look_here_first: FIRST FIND THE VERY SMALL, ROUNDED LEAVES, not the gland. E. simulans is a mostly hairless, prostrate or reclining spurge (5–40 cm), with OPPOSITE tiny oval to almost circular leaves only 1–3.2 mm long, ENTIRE edges, usually nearly symmetrical rounded bases and inconspicuous veins apart from the midvein. Look at one tiny cyathium at a distal node with a 10–30× lens: 4 red-purple ELLIPTIC slightly cupped glands but NO white petal-like APPENDAGES (versus E. golondrina's circular cupped glands WITH white crescents). A mature four-angled seed is 1.5–2 mm with 5–7 FAINT transverse ridges. E. theriaca var. theriaca is particularly hard to tell apart in the field and tends to have smaller seeds with 2–4 STRONG ridges; do not force species ID from a casual leaf photo.

taxonomic_note: Accepted Euphorbia simulans per POWO and Flora of North America. Not interchangeable with E. polycarpa or E. theriaca; older varietal names can complicate photo searches. FNA reports Texas records from Brewster, Hudspeth and Presidio counties; do not present as a documented Hays plant.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae, Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum: opposite usually unequal leaves, cyathia rather than ordinary flowers, and 3-lobed capsule that dries and releases seeds.
morphology_keys.habit: Annual or short-lived perennial; usually slender taproot/rootstock; prostrate to reclining glabrous branches about 5–40 cm, growing in arid desert scrub and rocky or sandy ground.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, ORBICULATE, OVAL or very short oblong, 1–3.2 × 1.5–5 mm; margins entire, rounded base usually SUBSYMMETRIC (unusual for many sandmats), tip rounded or occasionally notched, glabrous. Usually only midvein conspicuous.
morphology_keys.stipules: Distinct thin awl-shaped (subulate) glabrous scales, 0.5–0.7 mm, at leaf junctions. Distinguish from hairs under a strong lens; existing habit photograph cannot prove individual stipules.
morphology_keys.cyathia: Usually solitary at distal nodes on 0.3–0.7 mm stalks. Cup-like involucre 0.8–1.2 × 0.7–1 mm glabrous; 4 RED TO PURPLE slightly concave ELLIPTIC glands roughly 0.2–0.3 × 0.4–0.5 mm; appendages ABSENT. No white petal-like crescents expected.
morphology_keys.capsules: Broadly ovoid 3-lobed glabrous capsules 1.3–1.8 × 1.5–2 mm; this is compatible with golondrina and cannot resolve both species alone.
morphology_keys.seeds: WHITISH COAT OVER REDDISH-BROWN underneath; narrowly oblong, distinctly 4-angled, 1.5–2 × 1.3–1.8 mm, usually 5–7 FAINT shallow transverse ridges/wrinkles. E. theriaca var. theriaca commonly has smaller seeds with 2–4 PROMINENT transverse ridges. Mature seed macro with calibrated scale needed.
best_field_traits: Very tiny opposite nearly ROUND, entire-margined hairless leaves (1–3.2 mm long)
Subsymmetrical rounded leaf bases unlike strongly oblique leaves of many Chamaesyce
Cyathium at distal node, purple ELLIPTIC glands with NO white appendages
Distinct thin 0.5–0.7 mm glabrous subulate stipules
Mature 1.5–2 mm 4-angled seed with 5–7 weak transverse ridges; essential for close E. theriaca comparison

comparisons.key_distinctions: E. golondrina typically has larger and longer 5–11.5 × 1–4 mm narrow oblong leaves and WHITE crescent appendages around ROUND deeply cupped red-purple glands. E. simulans has VERY SHORT 1–3.2 mm rounded leaves and ELLIPTIC glands WITHOUT such appendages. E. theriaca is the genuinely difficult desert pair: its smaller seeds have around 2–4 prominent cross ridges versus simulans 1.5–2 mm seeds with 5–7 LOW weak ridges. E. serpens has rooting nodes and broad fused stipules, smaller smooth seeds; E. prostrata usually has hairy capsule keels and strongly cross-ridged seeds.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: E. simulans: tiny rounded leaves, appendage-free glands, and true seed
steps: Take a WHOLE prostrate plant photo with cm ruler and several stem tips; this is an arid West Texas species, not a presumed Hays common weed.
Zoom on leaf PAIRS: blades orbiculate/oval only 1–3.2 mm, ENTIRE edge, more symmetric base; confirm not a similarly small seedling.
At 15–30× isolate the RED-PURPLE elliptical gland of a single CYATHIUM: no white petal-like appendage should be present. Compare the documented white crescents in E. golondrina.
Turn over the true LEAF NODE for separate 0.5–0.7 mm narrow stipules (not incidental leaf hairs or mineral crystals).
Photograph separately a glabrous 3-lobed ripe capsule, then collect and verify an actual MATURE SEED (if permitted).
Under a calibrated 1 mm scale compare 1.5–2 mm seeds with 5–7 low ridges against E. theriaca var. theriaca smaller seeds with 2–4 stronger ridges.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: E. simulans and E. theriaca var. theriaca can be nearly impossible to separate from whole habit alone according to FNA. A blurry photo showing hairless stems and tiny leaves is suggestive, not confirmed. Don't label fine stipules, absence of appendages, mature seed ridges or capsule hairs unless actual photo allows it. Native-by-county certification remains paused.
